title: Minimality of an affine Betti-rank model over the affine residue field
statement: Let W be a scheme, E a derived module complex on W, w a point, and U an affine open containing w. Work with fixed derived categories as in [def-pc-derived-category]. Let K be a bounded complex on the localized open module site, with an isomorphism from E restricted to U to Q(K). Suppose K^j is a finite free sheaf of rank derivedFiberBetti(W,E,j,w) in every integer degree [def-sc-derived-fiber-betti, def-pc-perfect-complex]. Put A=Gamma(W,U), rho=evaluation at w and p=ker(rho) [def-weil-residue-field]. Every section differential K^j to K^(j+1), extended from A to kappa(p), is zero. No direct-image geometry, finite-residue-cohomology assumption, connectivity, or source basis is required.

source.document: Stacks Project, More on Morphisms and Derived Categories of Schemes

proof.text: Apply the affine free residue section cohomology comparison to K. Free section bases and scalar extension show each residue term is finite-dimensional of the prescribed Betti rank.

The cycles inclusion is injective; its homology projection is surjective. Finiteness of the term implies finiteness of cycles and homology. The two finrank inequalities and the rank hypothesis make the cycles inclusion surjective. Cancel it in iCycles_d to show every residue differential is zero.

For each coordinate in a finite free basis of the target section module, extend its evaluation map using the scalar-extension adjunction. The zero differential over kappa(w) makes every original coordinate evaluation zero. Its coordinate thus lies in p and has zero image in kappa(p). Tensor the target basis to kappa(p), distribute tensor over the finite coordinate product, and apply the tensor right unitor. Every coordinate of every pure-tensor differential vanishes. Tensor induction yields zero on every element.
